mechanism: scriptpubkey-desc (src/rpc/descriptors.lisp:2047-2056) is a two-way decision: script->address (:2039-2045, a case over classify-script covering pubkeyhash, scripthash, witness-v0-keyhash, witness-v0-scripthash and witness-v1-taproot) yields addr(<address>), and everything else falls to raw(<hex>). Core's InferScript (refs/bitcoin/src/script/descriptor.cpp:2691-2831 at d3056bc), which is what the desc field runs through InferDescriptor with DUMMY_SIGNING_PROVIDER (core_io.cpp:409-415, ScriptToUniv), tries the TYPED inferences first and only reaches ExtractDestination -> AddressDescriptor and then RawDescriptor after they all fail: TxoutType::PUBKEY at TOP/P2SH/P2WSH becomes pk(<hex>) (:2705-2710), TxoutType::MULTISIG becomes multi(k,<hex>,...) (:2731-2744), and a WITNESS_V1_TAPROOT output whose x-only key IsFullyValid becomes rawtr(<xonly>) once GetTaprootSpendData finds nothing (:2772-2802). None of those three needs key material, so the dummy provider does not suppress them.
consequence: The desc field disagrees with Core for P2PK, bare multisig and every taproot output on gettxout (src/rpc/blockchain.lisp:722-724), getblock verbosity 2/3 plus decoderawtransaction and getrawtransaction verbose (output-to-json, src/rpc/blockchain.lisp:516) and /rest/getutxos (src/rpc/rest.lisp:266-268). A tool that round-trips the field into importdescriptors still gets a watch-only descriptor covering the same script -- raw() and addr() both do -- so there is no funds effect; what is lost is the key and threshold Core reports, which is what a wallet-import or an indexer keys on. Bounded output divergence, hence S3. NOTE: the finding's impact text also names scantxoutset; that is wrong for our tree. Our scantxoutset echoes the caller's own descriptor back (src/rpc/descriptors.lisp:2255 reads a needles table), so it never calls scriptpubkey-desc and does not diverge here.

fix_shape: Give scriptpubkey-desc Core's ordered chain instead of the addressable/not split, driving it off the classify-script result it can already get: :pubkey with a valid pubkey -> pk(<hex>); :multisig -> multi(<m>,<hex>,...) from the solved :m and :pubkeys; :witness-v1-taproot whose 32-byte program is a fully valid x-only key -> rawtr(<xonly>); and only then the existing script->address -> addr(), with raw(<hex>) last. Keep the validity guards Core has, because they are what the two matching controls depend on: a hybrid-key P2PK must stay raw() (Core's InferPubkey rejects header 06/07), and a taproot program that is not a valid x-only key must fall through to addr(), since Core only builds RawTRDescriptor when pubkey.IsFullyValid(). The P2SH/P2WSH/tr()-tree arms of InferScript need a solving provider we do not pass here and should stay out of scope. Reuse descriptor-add-checksum unchanged. A regression test should assert all four Core vectors at descriptor_tests.cpp:1147-1157 plus a bare multisig and a rawtr case, keeping the two raw()/addr() controls so a change that simply always emits a typed descriptor cannot pass.
